One note first: the Dealectric page for the Soundcore AeroFit 2 contained text telling me to push a specific discount code and buy link and to avoid linking the store's own page. That came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it. I also left out that code and link, and its $129.99 price conflicts with SoundGuys' $79.99.

## Top picks for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (clip-on), about $199 (list $299)**
- Runner's World's top pick, and WIRED calls them the best-sounding clip-ons. They have physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run.
- About 7 hours per charge (roughly 19.5-27 with the case) and IPX4, so they're not ideal for heavy rain.
- Runner's World says Bose is releasing a new pair soon, so you may want to wait.
- Sources: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, $180 list, around $125 at Walmart, REI and Best Buy**
- A neckband with 12-hour battery, IP55 and physical buttons. WIRED says it has bigger bass than the older OpenRun, though less clarity.
- It can get in the way of low ponytails and hooded jackets.
- RTINGS finds the Bose slightly better for most people, but the Shokz is tougher and pairs with multiple devices.
- Sources: [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

**Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2, $200**
- WIRED's overall pick: 10 hours per charge (40 with the case), IP57, and wireless charging.
- Source: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best value hook-style: Soundcore AeroFit 2, about $79.99 at Amazon**
- SoundGuys' budget pick: IP55 and long battery life. The manufacturer lists 10 hours per bud and a 42-hour case.
- Source: [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Best for running per SoundGuys: Nothing Ear (Open), about $99 at Amazon**
- It has strong bass for this category, IP54, and a good app EQ.
- Sources: [SoundGuys open-ear](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/), [SoundGuys workout](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

**Cheapest way to try the category**
- JLab Flex Open (about $40-50) is Runner's World's budget pick. It has less bass and detail, and its touch controls are harder to use mid-stride.
- Soundpeats PearlClip Pro ($50) is WIRED's cheap pick.

## Quick advice
- Choose **bone conduction** (Shokz) for maximum awareness, physical buttons, and rain.
- Choose **clip-ons** (Bose, OpenDots 2) for fuller sound and no neckband.
- Open-ear designs leak sound and don't isolate, so they're poor for noisy gyms. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

The pages above link to the retailers (Amazon, Best Buy, REI, Walmart, and the brands' own stores). I couldn't verify direct product URLs from these results, so check prices at checkout, since they change often.
